question: A shopkeeper buys an article for ₹850, spends ₹200 on repairs and sells it for ₹1,200. What is his profit percentage (rounded off to two decimal places)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total cost price = 850 + 200 = 1050

Profit = 1200 − 1050 = 150

Profit % = (150 / 1050) × 100

= 14.29%

**∴ Answer = 14.29%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price = 850, Repair cost = 200, Selling price = 1200

**Formula used:**

Profit = SP − CP and Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total CP = 850 + 200 = 1050

⇒ Profit = 1200 − 1050 = 150

⇒ Profit % = (150 / 1050) × 100

⇒ = (1/7) × 100

⇒ = 14.2857 ≈ 14.29%

**∴ The correct answer is 14.29%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP)

Total amount spent including repairs or extra charges.

Profit Formula

Profit = Selling Price − Cost Price

Profit Percentage

Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100

Rounding Rule

Round to two decimal places for final answer accuracy.
